title: Finding record
description: One accessibility barrier, or one thing a person must check, observed on one element in one page state. Every check, agent and tester session emits this shape. A finding is an observation and never changes; its lifecycle (open, fixed, verified) lives in the ledger.

id.description: Fingerprint of where and what, so the same barrier found twice gets the same id. Computed by kuebiko.contracts.finding_id; see contracts/README.md.

run_id.description: The run that produced this record.

created_at.description: UTC time in ISO 8601 form, ending in Z.

app.description: Corpus key (owner/name from corpus/manifest.csv) or a short name for any other target.

url.description: The page as loaded, including host and port.

repo.description: Source repository as owner/name, when known.

commit.description: Full commit hash of the source that was running, when known.

state.description: How to reach the page state where the barrier appears, so a fix can be re-tested by script and by a person.

steps.description: Steps to replay after loading target.url. Empty when the barrier is visible on load.

description.description: The state in plain words, for example: checkout form after submitting with an empty email.

element.description: The element the finding is about, or null for a finding about the whole page.

selector.description: A CSS selector that matches exactly this element in this state.

html.description: The element's opening tag and as much of its content as fits.

name.description: The computed accessible name, which may be empty.

source_hint.description: Where the element comes from in source, when it can be traced.

id.description: Namespace and name of the check, for example axe:image-alt or kuebiko:focus-order.

source.description: rule: a deterministic check. agent: a model's verdict with evidence. tester: a person in a session.

model.description: The model that judged, for agent findings.

act_rule.description: Id of the W3C ACT rule this check implements, when there is one.

outcome.description: failed: the barrier is there. cantTell: a person has to decide. Passes are not findings; they are counted per criterion in run.json.

confidence.description: confirmed: a deterministic check or a person observed it. judged: a model concluded it from the evidence attached. needs-person: nobody has decided yet.

severity.description: blocker: the task cannot be completed. serious: it can, with real difficulty. moderate and minor: friction.

summary.description: One plain sentence saying what is wrong and for whom.

evidence.description: What supports the finding. At least one item.

remediation_hint.description: A short suggestion for the fix. Never a claim that the fix is sufficient.

tester.description: Present only for findings from a session. Holds no names or contact details.

setup.description: The assistive technology and settings used, for example NVDA on Windows or keyboard only. Never a diagnosis.

synthetic.description: true for scripted sessions and sessions run by the project's own maintainers.

extensions.description: Free-form space for experiments. Nothing may depend on it across workstreams.

allOf.description: A rule finding is always a confirmed failure.
An agent finding is judged or handed to a person, never confirmed.
A tester finding is a confirmed failure and carries the session.
needs-person and cantTell always go together.

key.description: Key name for press, for example Tab or Enter.

url.description: For goto. A path on the target's own origin, starting with a single slash, so ids do not change with host or port. A second slash or a backslash after the first would reach another origin.

allOf.description: Each action carries what it needs to be replayed.

path.description: File under the run's artifacts directory, relative to the run directory. No '..' segments and no backslashes, so it cannot point outside that directory.
